method: Read exact Gujarati and English blocks, record reverse paraphrase for quantifiers, directions, domain restrictions, proof assumptions and exceptions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Each domain element is assigned an element of the codomain. The range consists only of attained values.
samples.assessment: Domain, codomain and range remain distinct.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Different expressions define the same function when all argument values agree and the domain and codomain are shared.
samples.assessment: Extensional equality depends on the stated same-domain/codomain proviso.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every input must be in exactly one case. Exhaustiveness and exclusivity may need proof.
samples.assessment: Both coverage and uniqueness requirements retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The selector is the nonnegative principal square root because the natural-number domain includes zero.
samples.assessment: Corrected positive-at-zero wording is disclosed next to the example and leaves the preceding positive-integer two-root claim unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The example uses x consistently as the input and returns x+1.
samples.assessment: One n-to-x token correction is disclosed and keyed in structural parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Surjection means every codomain y has at least one domain x with f(x)=y.
Injection means each codomain y has at most one domain preimage; it need not have any.
A relation with a unique output wherever related and an output for every domain input is the graph of a total function.
samples.assessment: Both functionality and totality hypotheses kept.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Functions can be treated as graphs for mathematical convenience, without a metaphysical identity claim; the graph is typed as a relation contained in A times B.
samples.assessment: Both conditional reader branches translated; OLFUN-004 terminology repair disclosed in the same aligned block.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Restriction changes the domain to C and keeps values on C. Application to C returns the set of attained values.
samples.assessment: The explicit domain-only function restriction remains unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Function restriction is analogous to relation restriction but acts only on the input coordinate, while the earlier homogeneous relation restriction acts on both coordinates.
samples.assessment: The source claim of exact identity is qualified and the distinction is disclosed.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An inverse B to A undoes f in both orders on all of A and B.
samples.assessment: Both compositions and domain ranges retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For an injection with nonempty domain, choose the unique preimage on the range and a fixed domain element outside the range.
samples.assessment: The theorem and proof now state the needed nonempty-domain condition; OLFUN-001 also discloses the empty-to-singleton counterexample and exact general condition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A surjection admits a right inverse by selecting one preimage for each codomain element. This assumes choice in general; finite or natural-number domain, and bijections, are exceptions.
samples.assessment: Footnote, both future-chapter branches and no-choice singleton argument all retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A function has at most one two-sided inverse.
The composition of f with g applies f first, then g: g(f(x)).
samples.assessment: Order preserved despite notation macro arguments f,g.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A partial function assigns at most one output to each ambient A input. Its domain is the subset where it is defined.
samples.assessment: Ambient source set and defined domain are not conflated.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A functional relation defines a partial function, and seriality additionally makes it total.
samples.assessment: Serial means every source element has a target, not an ordered sequence.
